title: The hypertrophy series: the primordial metric for muscle growth
summary: NH explains why tonnage is his central metric: frequency, volume and intensity form a trinity, and quality tonnage is what they produce together. He argues that natural size comes from accumulating tonnage over years, that bodybuilders who chase strength end up smaller than those who chase tonnage, and that all programming principles feed into it like streams into an ocean.
claims: Tonnage is by nature the most important aspect of programming and progression, not a gimmick of his
Frequency, volume and intensity together create tonnage; isolating one as the key factor for hypertrophy breaks up a trinity
High volume and frequency without work in relevant intensity windows produces low-quality tonnage
Intensity and frequency without volume gives high-quality tonnage but too little of it
Without frequency you cannot repeat tonnage accumulation through the week, and you lose intensity because a single day holds limited quality work
No single week of training produces big gains for a natural; volume in a week or month is tiny next to lifetime accumulation
Picture weekly volume poured into a large container whose contents are tonnage, filling from the day you start training
Naturals with the best physiques have very high lifetime tonnage, in the millions of pounds
Tonnage accumulation needs patience and time and cannot be forced
Forcing tonnage means either constant high-intensity work with little accumulation, or junk volume with baby weights
Raising tonnage numbers alone does not guarantee growth: going from 10 to 100 million pounds with 40-50 rep baby-weight sets could yield very little
Two lifters who both take their squat from 100 to 300 lb will differ in size: the one who focused on intensity gets there first, the one who focused on tonnage ends up bigger
Bodybuilders should not chase strength as a goal; doing so makes you train like a powerlifter, strong but without the muscle to show for it
Every programming tool he uses leads to tonnage: volume, intensity, frequency, baseline and intensity windows are streams that end in the ocean of tonnage
Tonnage is simply reps times weight, but you must understand the end goal, which is size, and stay within the windows the series describes
The series is around 60 episodes in; later episodes will be more niche and advanced
